news.title: Crypto Weekly: Bitcoin's rise, crypto-backed midterms
news.summary:
STORY: From Bitcoin's rise to crypto-backed midterms.

This is Crypto Weekly.

:: Crypto Weekly

:: Bitcoin powers on

Bitcoin rose above $80,000 to hit a more than three-month high...

as a soft U.S. dollar, in the wake of the moves by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to calm the bond market, revived momentum in the crypto sector.

Donald Trump last week called on Congress to pass a bill that would bring clearer definitions to the growing sector.

Since then, bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, has risen 16%.

:: Stablecoin spending spree

Global stablecoin card spending is expected to quadruple to $50 billion a year by 2028.

That was according to a stablecoin payments company RedotPay.

The Hong Kong-based firm said the projection comes as stablecoin card spend crossed $1 billion in July.

Global adoption of stablecoins has accelerated in recent years...

as they gain traction in cross-border ‌payments, treasury operations, and as a store of value in volatile economies.

:: Iran sanctions

The US announced what it called "an economic onslaught" against Iran...

combining new sanctions with threats against Tehran's trading partners.

It did not list specific countries that would be targeted.

But the newly listed activities include dealings in digital assets like crypto, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.

:: Midterm elections backing

Stand With Crypto, an advocacy group backed by Coinbase endorsed 32 incumbent congressional candidates for the November midterm elections,,,

as the industry cements influence in Washington.

The endorsements come as the Clarity Act, the crypto industry's top policy priority, stalls in the Senate.

Stand With Crypto hopes to return industry-friendly candidates to office.
